**What I did:** Determined liner diameter and length, as well as housing length and diameter\
**Note:** Log generated by Claude code, but concepts were worked out by me

# 2026-10-14: Liner and annulus sizing

## Decisions

| Part | Value | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Liner wall thickness | 2.5 mm | Stick welding limit (thinner stock burns through at 20–40 A) |
| Liner diameter | 76 mm OD / 71 mm ID | Trade-off: zone lengths, exit speed, housing size, stock tube |
| Primary zone length | 70 mm | 2.3 ms residence time |
| Secondary zone length | 60 mm | 1.6 ms residence time |
| Dilution zone length | 120 mm (1.7 D) | Mixing distance, 2.5 ms |
| **Liner length** | **250 mm** | **~6.3 ms total residence time** |
| Housing diameter | 108 mm OD / 103 mm ID | Annulus speed ~26 m/s |
| Annulus gap | 13.5 mm | Annulus dynamic pressure = 7.6 % of liner ΔP |
| Housing length | Liner + head-end plenum + ~5 mm slip clearance + exit transition | Plenum length still open |

## 1. Liner length: residence time per zone

Each zone must hold the gas long enough for its job to finish:

$$\tau = \frac{L}{V}, \qquad V = \frac{\dot m}{\rho A} \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad L = \tau \cdot V$$

- **A** is the liner's internal cross-section, π/4 × 0.071² = 0.00396 m². The gas travels along the tube
  through this area. The holes only set how much gas is in each zone (ṁ).
- **ṁ** is the gas flowing through the zone: cumulative zone air + all the fuel. Cooling film is neglected.
- **ρ** is the hot gas density at the zone temperature and liner pressure (P3 − ΔP ≈ 233 kPa),
  ρ = P/(R·T), R ≈ 288 J/kg·K. The gas expands as it heats, so it moves faster through the same tube.

| Zone | ṁ | T | ρ | V | Target τ | Length chosen | Actual τ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary | 0.0426 kg/s | 2337 K | 0.347 kg/m³ | 31.1 m/s | ~2 ms | 70 mm | 2.3 ms |
| Secondary | 0.0693 kg/s | 1777 K | 0.456 kg/m³ | 38.4 m/s | ~1.5 ms | 60 mm | 1.6 ms |
| Dilution | 0.2146 kg/s | → 880 K | → 0.92 kg/m³ | 38 → 59 m/s | mixing | 120 mm | ~2.5 ms |

**Why these residence times:**
- **Primary, ~2 ms:** propane at φ ≈ 1 reacts in ~0.1 ms. 2 ms gives about 20× margin against blowout.
- **Secondary, ~1.5 ms:** CO burnout at ~1800 K needs on the order of 1–2 ms.
- **Dilution:** set by mixing, not chemistry. The jets need distance to blend into an even temperature
  before the turbine. Rule of thumb: 1.5–1.8 liner diameters → 120 mm (1.7 D).

**Conservative:** these assume plug flow (gas moving straight through). The recirculation bubble holds
primary-zone gas longer than 2.3 ms, so the real margin is larger.

## 2. Liner diameter: a trade-off

The diameter is chosen, not derived. A narrower liner speeds the gas up; a wider one slows it down.

| Liner ID | Primary gas speed | Exit gas speed | Primary length for 2 ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60 mm | 43.5 m/s | 82 m/s | 87 mm (1.45 D) |
| 65.5 mm | 36.5 m/s | 69 m/s | 73 mm (1.11 D) |
| **71 mm** | **31.1 m/s** | **59 m/s** | **62 mm (0.87 D)** |
| 84 mm | 22.2 m/s | 42 m/s | 44 mm (0.53 D) |

**Why 71 mm ID:**
- **Two independent methods agree.** The residence-time lengths match standard combustor proportions
  (primary ≈ 0.75–1.0 D). At 60 mm the primary would need 1.45 D; at 84 mm only 0.53 D.
- **Exit speed ~59 m/s**, the same order as the compressor discharge (~47–51 m/s), so the turbine sees
  gas at a speed it was designed for. 60 mm would push 82 m/s into the turbine.
- **Compact housing (~108 mm)**, and 76 mm is a common tube size.
- **ID = OD − 2 × 2.5 mm** (wall thickness set by welding).

## 3. Annulus gap: annulus speed target

The annulus is the ring between the housing's inner wall and the liner's outer wall. It carries all the
compressor air to the holes. Sized from continuity at a target annulus speed:

$$A_{an} = \frac{\dot m}{\rho_3 V_{an}} \quad\Rightarrow\quad D_{housing,ID} = \sqrt{\frac{4A_{an}}{\pi} + D_{liner,OD}^2}$$

with ρ3 = 2.118 kg/m³ (compressor discharge air) and target V_an ≈ 25–30 m/s.

| Annulus speed | Housing ID | Gap | Dynamic pressure / ΔP |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25 m/s | 104.3 mm | 14.1 mm | 6.8 % |
| 30 m/s | 100.1 mm | 12.1 mm | 9.8 % |
| **26.4 m/s (chosen)** | **103 mm** | **13.5 mm** | **7.6 %** |

**Chosen:** housing 108 mm OD / 103 mm ID (2.5 mm wall), giving an annulus area of 37.96 cm².

## 4. Why the annulus dynamic pressure must stay under ~10 % of the liner ΔP

Moving air splits its pressure into **static** (pushes on walls) and **dynamic** (½ρV², tied up in motion).
**Holes are driven by static pressure**, because the static pressure difference across the wall is what
pushes air through.

As annulus air flows along the liner, every row of holes removes some of it, so it slows down and dynamic
pressure turns back into static. If the annulus air is fast:
- **Upstream holes** see lower static pressure → less ΔP → less air than designed.
- **Downstream holes** see higher static pressure → more ΔP → more air than designed.
- Fast air must turn sharply to enter a hole, **lowering the real C_d** below the assumed 0.6.

Keeping annulus dynamic pressure small next to ΔP keeps both effects small: every hole sees nearly the
same ΔP, so the air split and hole areas work as calculated. **~10 % is a rule of thumb, not a law.**

$$q_{an} = \tfrac{1}{2}(2.118)(26.4)^2 \approx 738 \text{ Pa} = 7.6\% \text{ of } \Delta P \;(9{,}727 \text{ Pa})$$

## 5. Why the gap is sized at the inlet end

The annulus carries **all** the air at the inlet end. Each row of holes removes some, so with a constant
gap the air slows down further along:

| Location in annulus | Air still flowing | Speed |
|---|---|---|
| Inlet end | 100 % | 26.4 m/s |
| After primary holes + cooling | 76 % | ~20 m/s |
| After secondary holes + cooling | 61 % | ~16 m/s |

The inlet end has the fastest air and largest dynamic pressure, so it's the worst case. If it meets the
10 % rule, every point downstream does too.

**Assumes** air enters near the head (flange) end and flows toward the turbine. If the side inlet sits
mid-length, air flows both ways and this must be redone.

## 6. Housing length

Not simply "a few mm longer than the liner." The housing must contain:
- **Head-end plenum:** space where inlet air slows down before reaching the first holes (see risk 1).
- **Liner:** 250 mm.
- **Slip clearance:** ~5 mm. At ~800 °C the 304 liner grows ~3 mm in length (α ≈ 18 × 10⁻⁶ /K, ΔT ≈ 700 K)
  and ~1 mm in diameter, while the cooler housing grows less.
- **Exit transition** to the turbine inlet flange.

**Thermal expansion is handled by the attachment:** liner welded at the flange end only; the turbine end
slides in a loose-fit sleeve. If both ends are fixed, the liner buckles or cracks.

## Assumptions

| Assumption | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Liner pressure | P3 − ΔP ≈ 233 kPa | 4 % liner pressure drop |
| Hot gas R | 288 J/kg·K | Combustion products ≈ air |
| Zone temperatures | Cantera equilibrium values | Primary 2337 K, secondary 1777 K |
| Flow model | Plug flow, cooling film neglected | Conservative for residence time |
| Annulus speed target | 25–30 m/s | Keeps q_an < ~10 % of ΔP |
| Dilution length | 1.5–1.8 D | Combustor rule of thumb |

## Risks and open items

- [ ] **Side inlet jet:** compressor air enters through the 50 mm stub at ~51 m/s, with dynamic pressure
      ≈ 2,750 Pa (28 % of ΔP). If it hits the liner directly, holes facing the inlet get more air than the
      far side. Fix: head-end plenum or baffle so air reaches the holes at annulus speed. Check in SimScale.
- [ ] **Slip joint** at the turbine end of the liner: design the sleeve and clearance in CAD.
- [ ] **Head-end plenum length:** depends on the inlet fix; sets total housing length.
- [ ] **Stock sizes:** confirm 76 × 2.5 mm and 108 × 2.5 mm 304 tube at Ferik Steel / GPS. If different,
      rerun gas speeds and gap.
- [ ] **Exit transition:** 71 mm liner to the turbine housing inlet (T3 divided flange on the HX35 reference).
- [ ] Set `liner_diameter_mm = 76` in chamber_calc.py and pick hole count × diameter per row.

## Naming correction

Compressor discharge velocity (~47 m/s in the 52 mm outlet, ~51 m/s in the 50 mm stub) belongs to
**station 3**, not station 2. Station 2 is the compressor inlet. Earlier "V2" entries should read V3.
